description: The same rush team on both sides of a 6-row gap: the battle stays symmetric.
A rush (two barracks) against a base with only a wall and its Core; soldiers walk across and destroy the Core.
A Core walled in on all sides (one weak wall, tier 1): the soldiers break through the weakest wall and reach the Core.

A Core ringed by eight tier 1 walls and two soldiers walking in from the gap: the battle is saved and restored (JSON round trip) after 50, 95, 130 and 200 ticks (before and after the first wall takes damage, and after it falls), and ends exactly like an uninterrupted run (the breach field depends only on the saved state).

Three raiders (placed at tick 0) walk past the extractor and the splitter of a base to its Core (issue #66: no unit prefers buildings): nothing is destroyed, the barracks downstream keeps producing, and the two sides fight at the Core.

Three powered tier 2 turrets beside the front edge kill three soldiers that cross it after a long walk across a 12-row gap, by which time the turrets are charged (they fire only once a unit stands on their own board rows).
Three powered tier 3 turrets on the front row shoot and kill a soldier that is still in the 12-row neutral zone (PP-13): it never reaches the turret owner's board rows.
The same three turrets without any supply never fire; the soldiers walk in and attack the Core.

A wall line with one gate: a soldier inside walks out through the gate (standing on its cell) while an enemy soldier outside cannot enter and attacks the gate, until the owning soldier comes out and kills it.
Eight tier 1 turrets; a lake band and walls leave a single approach (x = 8) right above them, so a twelve-soldier wave runs the gauntlet.

A fast flux extractor feeds a tier 1 overclocker (costPerStep 4, +5 percent per step); the ore extractor beside it, which feeds a barracks, speeds up step by step (ore items at 19, 39, 59, 78, 96, ...).

Two plots. Player 0 has the ore extractor and barracks and the flux extractor feeding a tier 1 overclocker (as in ramp-overclocker-speeds-source); player 1 has a lone ore extractor in their own plot (ore node at x 12, not connected, so its items are lost at its own cadence) and no overclocker. Player 0's collectors speed up step by step; player 1's extractor stays on the unmodified cadence (PP-8).
An armory (costPerStep 6, +4 percent per step) beside a barracks: the soldiers spawned at ticks 119, 239, 359 have 40, 41 and 43 health; units already on the field keep theirs.
A tier 1 overclocker (maxSteps 6) fed by a fast flux extractor reaches its sixth step and then takes nothing more: its buffer fills and the extractor stalls.

A base sealed by a wall row whose weakest point is an overclocker (a slow flux extractor feeds it): the attackers breach it and destroy it at tick 205, just after its fourth step; its bonus leaves the total at once.
Two Cores in wall rings and no producers: Overload decay (5 * level on every 100th tick from 1800) destroys both Cores at tick 3100 (cumulative 525 >= 500).

A Core ringed by six tier 3 walls and a soldier standing on the corner cell beside two of them (buildings 4 and 5, equal in everything but current health: building 5 starts at 20 of 240). The breach step prices a building by its maximum health, so both cost the same and the tie goes to building 4; the soldier never touches the damaged building 5 (a rule that used current health would chew through it).

Four soldiers of side 0 walk towards one stationary enemy (a unit_post): two start the same distance from it on either side, two at different distances. Overlapping units are pushed apart; the state hash pins every position.

Twelve soldiers of side 0 cross a wall line with a single one-cell gap (board row 8 of side 1). They crowd the gap, push through it (overlapping a little while they squeeze) and slide along the wall; the invariant (nothing inside a wall) holds on every tick, and the positions after 300 ticks are pinned.

A tier 1 barracks is walled in except for one cell, and a unit_post of its own side stands on that cell (held in place because an enemy unit_post in contact with it keeps both busy attacking): the finished unit cannot be placed, so the barracks holds it, stops drawing from its input buffer (the conduit backs up and the extractor stalls) and nothing is spawned in 700 ticks.

An ogre (collision radius 160, diameter 320 > one cell) and a soldier of side 0 head for a wall line with a one-cell gap: the soldier, nearer to the gap, passes and goes on to the Core; the ogre waits in front of the gap (the circle rules, not the cell field, stop it). Positions after 500 ticks are pinned.

Nine groups, apart from each other. In eight, a fast dart (side 0 or 1) aggroes on a stationary post of the other side whose centre it reaches in one step, so the two centres coincide; the unit ids give odd and even sums, the mover the higher or the lower id. In the ninth, two darts of equal priority reach the same post. Each pushed unit leaves along the separation axis in the frame of its own side (side 1 mirrors side 0); a harmless pin of the dart side keeps each post in contact (so anchored) without blocking the push. The positions pin the rule.
